title: Maybe You Should Talk To Someone

a: The issue they bring to therapy, which is often not the real one
The diagnosis a therapist writes after the first session
The fee a patient agrees to pay for treatment
The defense mechanism they use to avoid emotion
questions.why: Lesson 1 defines it as the problem a patient comes in hoping to solve, usually hiding a deeper issue.

questions.q: What did John’s case reveal beneath his insomnia and relationship complaints?
a: Unresolved grief from the deaths of his mother and young son
A medical condition that required medication rather than therapy
A conflict with his employer that he had not mentioned
A fear of being alone that began in his marriage
questions.why: Lesson 1 says six months passed before the traumatic losses behind John’s behavior emerged.

questions.q: Which defense mechanism did Gottlieb use after her boyfriend left her?
a: She fixated on his misdeeds during therapy sessions
She pretended the relationship had never mattered
She threw herself into caring for her patients
She refused to speak at all during sessions
questions.why: Lesson 2 describes her obsession with his wrongs as a way of avoiding the deeper pain.

questions.q: What deeper concern did Gottlieb’s therapist detect behind her breakup talk?
a: Distress about her life being half over and her own mortality
A desire to return to her former boyfriend immediately
Worry that she was unsuited to being a therapist
Anger at her friends for not supporting her
questions.why: Lesson 2 says remarks about her life being half over revealed fear about death, not just the relationship.

questions.q: What does “breaking open” mean in the summary?
a: Lowering your guard and facing repressed feelings head-on
Ending therapy when the sessions become too painful
Revealing a patient’s secrets to their family
Starting a new relationship before healing from the last
questions.why: Lesson 3 describes breaking open as acknowledging repressed emotion, which allows progress to begin.
